title: Xarra!
subtitle: Turn articles, books, and documents into audio you can follow.
description:
Import an article, PDF, DAISY book, document, or your own text, and Xarra turns it into natural-sounding audio with synchronized highlighting. Read along line by line, listen hands-free, or move between the two.

Bring content in from Safari, Files, the clipboard, a URL, or Project Gutenberg. Downloaded content remains available offline, while your library and listening progress can sync through your private iCloud.
nameOrigin: Xarra (pronounced "CHA-rra") comes from a Valencian/Catalan word meaning "to chat" or "to talk".
imageDescription: Xarra app icon - a stylized icon representing text to audio conversion

featuredIn.title: Create with Swift Weekly Newsletter #101 (Indie App of the Week)

featuredQuote: The app developed by Daniel is well integrated into the system. (...) Accessibility runs through the whole experience rather than sitting on top of it.
featuredQuoteSourceTitle: Create with Swift Weekly Newsletter #101 (Indie App of the Week)

features.title: Synchronized highlighting
features.description: As Xarra reads, the current line is highlighted. Optional word highlighting can use a background or underline, so you can choose the style that is easiest to follow.
features.imageDescription: Xarra on iPhone in Dark Mode, with the current paragraph outlined in purple and the word Accessibility highlighted within it.

features.title: Chapters and navigation
features.description: Detected headings become chapters you can jump between, making longer articles, DAISY books, and documents easier to explore.
features.imageDescription: Xarra on Mac with a Chapters window listing detected headings and listening progress for a longer article.

features.title: Resume anytime
features.description: Xarra saves your listening position automatically and can sync it through your private iCloud. Control playback from the Lock Screen or Control Center and continue when it suits you.
features.imageDescription: Screenshot of the iOS Control Center showing Xarra integrated with system media controls. The Now Playing tile displays artwork for an audio document titled “iOS 14: Custom Accessibility Content,” along with a pause button and skip backward and skip forward controls that move five lines at a time, indicating playback can be resumed and controlled from the Lock Screen and Control Center.

features.title: Tailored to each Apple device
features.description: Xarra is tailored for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Vision Pro: resizable iPad windows, Mac tabs and drag-and-drop, and Focus Mode on Vision Pro. Your library and progress can sync through iCloud.
features.imageDescription: Xarra on Apple Vision Pro in a room, with a translucent library-and-reader window, synchronized highlighting, playback controls, and Focus Mode.

features.title: Quick system integration
features.description: Share pages and documents from Safari, Notes, and other apps; import from Files; paste from the clipboard; type text; or add a URL. Once imported, Now Playing keeps playback close on the Lock Screen and in Control Center.
features.imageDescription: Xarra's iPad share extension showing a checkmark and the confirmation Saved to Xarra, indicating that shared content is ready to open in the app.

features.title: Smarter listening with Apple Intelligence
features.description: On supported devices, Apple Intelligence can summarize content, suggest tags and categories, and turn code blocks into natural, audio-friendly explanations. Imports and listening continue to work when those models are unavailable.
features.imageDescription: Xarra on Mac with an Edit Audio Document window showing Swift code, its detected programming language, and a plain-language explanation generated for listening.

features.title: Designed to work beautifully with assistive technologies
features.description: Xarra works thoughtfully with VoiceOver, Voice Control, Switch Control, and Full Keyboard Access. Navigation, playback, and reading remain usable across different interaction methods.
features.imageDescription: Screenshot of Xarra’s home screen with VoiceOver enabled. The VoiceOver cursor is focused on an Audio Document row titled “Welcome to Xarra,” highlighting the entire row. At the bottom of the screen, the Captions Panel displays VoiceOver’s spoken output for the focused element, showing the document title, source, and progress information.

features.title: Adaptive by default
features.description: Xarra respects Dynamic Type and Larger Text, Bold Text, Increase Contrast, Differentiate Without Color, Reduce Motion, and Light or Dark appearance. Choose System, OpenDyslexic, Atkinson Hyperlegible, or Lexend as your reading font.
features.imageDescription: Xarra on iPad with an accessibility text size enabled, showing a very large transcript line outlined in purple and large playback controls below.

features.title: Accessibility, made explicit
features.description: Accessibility shapes importing, reading, and listening rather than appearing as a separate mode. When an article supplies image alt text or captions, Xarra preserves that information in the readable and spoken content.
features.imageDescription: Side-by-side screenshot comparison. On the left, Safari displays a blog post containing an image of the VoiceOver rotor set to “More Content.” On the right, the same article is shown in Xarra, where the image’s alt text has been extracted and inserted inline into the text, making the image description readable and listenable as part of the article.

features.title: Text, links, and documents
features.description: Add articles and PDFs, import DAISY books, browse Project Gutenberg, share from another app, paste text, or enter a URL. Xarra extracts the readable content and prepares it for listening.
features.imageDescription: Xarra's iPad library with its Add menu open, offering Plain Text, URL, Document, and Gutenberg Library as import sources.

features.title: Voices and languages
features.description: Xarra detects the document language and lets you choose a preferred system voice for each language. It also guides you to Premium and Enhanced voices available through Apple settings.
features.imageDescription: Xarra on Mac with Voice settings open, showing automatic language detection, a Premium fallback voice, and preferred voices for English, Spanish, Catalan, and German.

features.title: Playback speed and preferences
features.description: Set the reading speed to match your pace, or ask Xarra to follow your device's assistive-technology voice and speech-rate settings.
features.imageDescription: Xarra on iPhone in Dark Mode, showing a highlighted paragraph and expanded playback controls with five-line skips, pause, and a 1.0 times speed setting.

whySection: Xarra is built to be helpful, respectful, and easy to trust. Downloaded content works offline, and your documents and listening progress can sync through your private iCloud when enabled. There are no ads, analytics, trackers, or separate Xarra account to create. The app stays focused on helping you engage with text in the way that works best for you.
supportText: Having trouble getting the most out of Xarra? We’re here to help you turn your text into the perfect audio experience!
